newsitem.title: UK: Cuba, Brazil feature again in sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Cuba, Brazil feature again in sugar freight orders.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a steady trickle of new enquiry on Wednesday as Cuba and south Brazil featured again as quoted origins, shipbrokers said.

Of the day's new orders, E D & F Man quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to Lagos for the end of May, while Pacol was in for 14,000 of bulk from its usual origin of Cuba to the Black Sea for any May dates.

Andre also issued a Cuban order for May, quoting for 14,000 tonnes to Baltic/Black Sea. Louis Dreyfus was in the market for a prompt 12,500/13,500 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo or east Africa.
Kerry was open for 10,000 tonnes of bulk sugar, five percent, from Thailand to Kunsan for the end of May.

Cargill, the subject of much market interest due to its large physical raws delivery from Paranagua against New York futures, featured on the freight market again with two new bagged orders and two fixtures.
It quoted for 14,000 tonne from east coast Mexico to Nigeria with options of Baltic, Mediterranean and Red Sea for mid-May and 10,000 tonnes from Visakhapatnam to Mediterranean for May 20/25.
Shipbrokers said Cargill fixed its recent order for 16,800 tonnes of bulk sugar from Rio Haina to US Gulf/Atlantic for May 15/23 and also 14,000 tonnes in bags from Coatzacoalcos to Callao.
Dreyfus fixed 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Continent to Tunisia for the end of May.
Elsewhere, heavy rains are reported to have interrupted loading of sugar and soy exports at Paranagua although loading at Santos has not been affected so far.

At Paranagua, two vessels were loading 14,000 tonnes of sugar in big bags apiece, while four other vessels were waiting to load 65,100 tonnes in big bags and two waiting to load 35,700 tonnes in bulk.
No sugar ships were docked at Santos but two were waiting to load 28,000 tonnes of bagged sugar.
